blesh-nightly.description: ble.sh publishes no usable releases -- its newest version tag predates the rolling `nightly` tag by years -- but every nightly build is kept as its own immutable asset stamped with a date and commit. No built-in datasource enumerates release assets, so this one reads them from the API and turns each into a version plus the digest GitHub publishes alongside it.

customManagers.description: Moves blesh_version and blesh_sha256 as one unit. The shared .chezmoidata manager above captures a single value per `# renovate:` annotation and so cannot express a version with its digest, which is why the data file carries no annotation and this matches the two keys by name instead.

Single files taken from a branch snapshot rather than a release, pinned by commit so the bytes cannot change under a refreshPeriod. The branch to follow is not recoverable from a pinned URL, so the annotation above each one carries it -- these two repos do not share a default branch.
Release assets downloaded by tag. The `releases/latest/download/` form these replace resolves at fetch time, so the version was whatever upstream had published that day.

mise.description: The deployed global mise fragments live under a chezmoi `dot_config` source path, which the manager's built-in patterns (keyed on a literal `.config`) can't match. Every fragment is kept as plain TOML rather than a chezmoi template so this manager can parse it, which is what makes per-dep `# renovate:` annotations unnecessary there; docs/mise.md carries the rationale. managerFilePatterns is additive, so the repo-root mise.toml keeps matching by default.

packageRules.description: Restrict noisy agent-skill digest updates to a single early-morning window on the 1st and 15th (America/Chicago). The narrow window keeps the snapshot of `main` to one PR per dep per cycle: daytime merges fall outside it, so a freshly-advanced `main` can't trigger a same-day follow-up PR.
